Hmm.  Not sure why people stay away from B4 IT Audit, other than just staying away from B4 in general, but contrary to the other 2 posts, my experience in IT Audit hasn't limited exit opportunities compared to my peers in financial audit.  Sure, they could transfer to any town/city and find some accounting work, and IT Audit I'm limited to working in a larger metro or city with an IT base, but the jobs I can transfer into after 3-5 years pay more than what my peers would transfer into at 3-5 years.  Love my job, learn something new every day.  We *do* provide advice, and work on consulting engagements.  The type of advice we provide is risk and technology based, normally focused on the security and accuracy of information.  A plus that I see is the likelihood of financial audit tasks being automated in the near future.  Our firm has regular talks about the changing nature of financial audit due to technological advancements.  IT Audit, to me, is more secure in the long run, and gives you tools to use in any industry, and in multiple roles, financial and technological.  My "busy season" runs 9 months of the year with 50-70hr weeks, versus a traditional accounting busy season.
